tasks.title: the ci.yml reader accepts only the call shapes it can read and refuses every other line that names the tool
tasks.description: Phase review round 4 (review-P87d.json). The reader still reads every line naming the tool and only exempts blocks whose key is spelled exactly `run:`, so "run": >, 'run': >, `run : >`, `&k run: >` read silently as no-flag (ci.yml's expected answer), a quoted one-line value is dropped, and `run: &a |`, `run: !!str >` or a deeper comment under a one-line run: are refused with a wrong message. Invert the rule into an allow-list: in YAML mode a line naming the tool is accepted only as (a) a one-line `run:` (optionally after `- `) whose unquoted value is the call, or (b) a line in the body of a block opened by a plain `run: |` (optionally `|-`/`|+`, trailing comment allowed). Every other non-comment line that names the tool is refused by line with the two accepted shapes named. A full-line comment is never a call and never extends a value. Pin each review shape (quoted keys, spaced key, anchored key, quoted value, anchored/tagged indicator, deeper comment) in ra29d or a new case: each is either read correctly or refused, none read silently. Re-wrap the manifest-conventions.md phase.merged bullet. Red first.

tasks.title: the call reader reads block-scalar context and counts only a word in command position as the call
tasks.description: Phase review round 5 (review-P87e.json). Two silent misreads remain. (1) The YAML reader checks line shapes, not context: a `run: <call>` line inside another key's block scalar (a `- name: >` body, `with: script: |`) is read as a step call. Track every block scalar (any key whose value opens with | or > after optional anchor/tag/indicators) and its body by indentation; a body that is not an accepted plain `run: |` is opaque - a tool-naming line inside it is refused by line, never read. State the allow-list as over YAML context, and fix the CHANGELOG/comment. (2) Any word ending in the tool path counts as the call, so `ls <tool>`, `git diff -- <tool>`, `echo see <tool>` read as a no-flag call (ci.yml's expected answer). Count a word as the call only in command position: the command word itself, or the word right after a python interpreter word (python, python3, python3.N, an absolute path to one) with no other argument between; a mention anywhere else is not a call. Add fixtures for both, red first, in both readers (shell and YAML) where they apply.

tasks.title: an exact call line is read only when its neighbouring lines leave it self-contained
tasks.description: Phase review round 7 (review-P87g.json). The exact-line pin reads each physical line alone, so the real call's own neighbours can change what runs. (1, med, regression of the deleted ra29c/ra29d) In YAML a flag on a continuation line of the run's own value is dropped: `- run: >`, `- run: >-`, and a plain `- run: <call>` continued on a deeper line read as ALL_ARMS (ci.yml's expected answer) while CI runs only --against-commit. Read a YAML call line only if (a) it is a one-line `run: <call>` whose next non-blank, non-comment line is indented no deeper than the run: key, or (b) the nearest earlier line indented less than it is a plain literal opener `run: |`, `|-` or `|+` (optionally after `- `); refuse anything else by line. (2, low) In shell, a call line continued from the line above (`echo "x" \`, `: \`) is read though the tool never runs: when the previous line ends in a backslash, read the call only if that line is exactly the runner's wrapper (`run "<label>" \`); otherwise refuse, naming both lines. Restore the folded and continued fixtures as ra29h rows with the flag on the continuation line; ra29h rows for `echo "x" \` + call and `: \` + call; a ra29g row keeping `run "x" \` + call as a read. The CHANGELOG and CONTRIBUTING sentences about a moved flag must match the code. Red first.

tasks.title: the tool compiles clean under -W error, invalid escapes fail the lint, and a call's whole continuation chain is checked
tasks.description: Phase review round 8 (review-P87h.json). (F1) P87.9 put an invalid escape (a backslash before a backtick) in _context_problem's docstring: every run on 3.12+ prints a SyntaxWarning and the file does not compile under -W error; default ruff (E9, F) cannot see it. Fix the docstring, and close the class: add W605 to [tool.ruff.lint] select in pyproject.toml so an invalid escape fails the lint gate; run ruff over plugins/audit and tools to confirm nothing else is red. (F2) The continuation check looks one line up only: `echo "x" \` or `: \` above the `run "<label>" \` wrapper, `true ||` above the wrapper or a call, and `false &&` above a call in a run: | body leave the real call read while it never runs. Walk the continuation chain: the wrapper's previous line, and the call's previous line when there is no wrapper, must not end in a backslash, `&&`, `||` or `|` (after stripping a trailing comment is not needed - a line ending in those is a continuation); otherwise refuse, naming the lines. The real tree's preceding lines do not, so ra29 stays green. Add ra29i rows for each shape. Red first for both (F1: compile under -W error::SyntaxWarning fails on the current file).

tasks.title: a trailing comment does not hide a continuation operator, and the pin states that reachability is not decided
tasks.description: Phase review round 9 (review-P87i.json). (1) A trailing comment after &&, || or | hides the token: `false && # skip`, `true || # c`, `echo x | # c` above the wrapper or a call leave the real call read while it never runs. Strip a trailing shell comment before testing &&, || and | (not before a backslash - `\ #` does not continue); ra29i rows for the three shapes, red first. (2) The section comment claims a line is refused whenever the lines around it mean it is not what runs, but a text check cannot decide reachability: `exit 0`, `false && {`, `if false; then ... fi` above the call are read, and the release arm itself depends on reading a call inside an if. Narrow the sentence to what is checked (the exact line, its own continuation chain, and its YAML context) and state the limit plainly in the comment and the CHANGELOG: whether the line is reached at all - control flow above it - is not decided by this check.

tasks.title: the line before a call's command is judged by a strict character rule, not a comment lexer
tasks.description: Phase review round 10 (review-P87j.json). The trailing-comment cut is a small shell lexer and leaks the same way the readers did: `false &&# c`, escaped quotes (`false \" && # c`), `false \ #x &&`, and a comment ending in a backslash above a blank line all leave the real call read. Do not write a lexer. Replace the continuation test with a strict character rule: the nearest earlier CODE line before the command's start (skipping blank lines and full-line comments - a line whose first non-space character is #, which never continues a command in shell) must contain none of the characters & | \ # anywhere; in ci.yml the plain `run: |` opener is the block's edge and is exempt. Any such line is refused by line, naming it. The real tree passes: verify.sh's lines before the plain and release wrappers and ci.yml's `set -e` contain none of them. Delete _without_trailing_comment and the operator-suffix logic the rule makes dead, and the docstring sentence about a backslash before a comment. ra29i rows for every round-10 spelling, red first; ra29g keeps full-line comments (including ones ending in a backslash or &&) and a plain command line above the call as reads. State in the comment and CHANGELOG that the rule is deliberately strict: a correct but unusual line above the call is refused loudly.

tasks.title: the runner files are split into lines the way the shell splits them
tasks.description: Phase review round 11 (review-P87k.json). The reader splits lines where the shell does not: run_arms opens with universal newlines (a lone CR becomes a newline) and call_lines/release_lines use str.splitlines(), which also breaks at VT, FF, FS-RS, NEL, LS and PS. So `: <FF>  python3 <tool> --against-commit` in place of the real call reads as the real call while the shell passes it to `:`. Read and split as the shell does: open with newline="" and split on "\n" only (one splitter for call_lines and release_lines, so release line numbers agree). Such a line then names the tool without equalling a call line and is refused by line; a CRLF call line keeps its CR and is refused too (correct: bash reads backslash-CR as no continuation). ra29h/ra29i rows for FF, CR and U+2028 under a `run "y" \` wrapper, each refused naming the line; a ra29b row where a FF inside the release block does not shift release_lines. Widen THE LIMITS sentence from heredoc/string/block text to any construct that makes the call line data rather than a command (array literal, arithmetic, a string opened on an earlier line), in the comment and CHANGELOG. Red first.
